audit.whatIsWrong: Sejuani wins 58.62% but the chart gave Neeko five stages and Sejuani none.
audit.why: Packet defect confirmed. Neeko genuinely owns levels 1-3 as a ranged poke laner with a 1000-range root, so those stay hers. But content.mid already says 'one good R erases her level 6 spike entirely' and content.late says she is 'fighting a champion she cannot kite and cannot burst through' — the chart never recorded either. Levels 4-5 flatten to Skill, Level 6 and the two-item stage go to Sejuani, and the first-item stage stays Skill because that is where her burst window is real.
audit.corrected: win[3]=Skill, win[4]=Sejuani, win[6]=Sejuani with matching phase sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike justified itself with 'a long-range stun she cannot dodge with W clone tricks'.
audit.why: The real reason Level 6 flips is stronger and it is in Riot's passive text: Inherent Glamour breaks when Neeko receives 'immobilizing crowd control'. Sejuani's whole kit is immobilizing crowd control. Glacial Prison does not merely hit through the clone puzzle — it deletes the disguise.
audit.corrected: Spike now states the disguise break.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] told the player to 'walk behind minions to block Tangle-Barbs'. whys[4] called Pop Blossom a channel you can stand through. content.mid called Sejuani's resistances 'passive Permafrost armor'.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs 'damages and roots everything it passes through. If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' Riot's text describes an ability that passes through what it hits and gets WORSE for doing so, so 'hide behind minions' is at best unsupported and at worst the exact opposite of the play — sidestepping is what the text supports. Pop Blossom is 'a short preparation' whose tell is HIDDEN while she is disguised, not a channel; the counter is breaking the disguise with CC before it starts. And Sejuani's resistances are Fury of the North / Frost Armor, not Permafrost.
audit.corrected: Sidestep advice replaces the minion-block advice, the preparation and its hidden tell are described accurately, and the passive is named correctly.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range, Blooming Burst 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 800, Shapesplitter 16/15/14/13/12s for free, Pop Blossom 120/105/90s.

edits.before: Glacial Prison gives you a long-range stun she cannot dodge with W clone tricks; one clean R into E shuts off her root window and starts the all-in.
edits.after: Any immobilizing CC breaks Inherent Glamour — one Glacial Prison strips her disguise, ends the clone puzzle, and opens the all-in she was hiding from.

edits.before: Walk behind minions to block Tangle-Barbs (E root) and deny her safe poke range all lane
edits.after: Sidestep Tangle-Barbs — it roots everything it passes through and grows after each champion

edits.before: Use Shapesplitter (W) clone disguises to bait your Arctic Assault (Q) into the fake target and reset her safe distance
edits.after: Use Shapesplitter (16s at rank 1) clone disguises to bait Arctic Assault into a fake target and reset her distance

edits.before: Pop Blossom (R) online gives her a devastating all-in setup through clone disguise — walk in as a minion or teammate, root, and channel while you have no way to stop it if your R is on cooldown.
edits.after: Pop Blossom's preparation is HIDDEN while she is disguised — but any immobilizing CC breaks Inherent Glamour, so a landed Permafrost or Glacial Prison takes the disguise and the surprise with it.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are still Neeko's best window — her poke sustains the lead and her W disguise makes every engage a guessing game. Sit behind the wave, let her push, and manage your passive Permafrost armor by not eating unnecessary poke before you want to trade. At 6, Glacial Prison changes the equation: she cannot clone-dodge a comet thrown at the real target, and a full R-into-E chain stuns her through the full Pop Blossom channel time — one good R erases her level 6 spike entirely. Bait the E root onto a minion before committing Q.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are her best window — Blooming Burst (7-9s) sustains the lead and Shapesplitter makes every engage a guessing game. Sit behind the wave, let her push, and keep Fury of the North's Frost Armor intact by refusing poke you did not want. At 6, Glacial Prison changes the equation: any immobilizing CC breaks Inherent Glamour, so the stun strips her disguise and the clone puzzle at once, and Pop Blossom's hidden preparation stops being hidden. Bait the Tangle-Barbs root onto a minion before committing Q.

edits.before: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs (Root): matchup-defining — The root sets up her whole burst — sidestep it behind minions. Count it out loud if you must. - Your Q dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs (E): 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range — it roots everything it passes through, so sidestep rather than screen it. - Blooming Burst (Q): 7-9s. - Shapesplitter (W): 16-12s, free. - Pop Blossom (R): 120/105/90s.

edits.before: Track Neeko’s Tangle-Barbs (Root): The root sets up her whole burst — sidestep it behind minions. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Inherent Glamour breaks on any immobilizing crowd control — your stun is the answer to the clone, not a guess at it.

edits.before: The root sets up her whole burst — sidestep it behind minions. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: The root sets up her whole burst, and it is 12s at rank 1 — sidestep it, then go.

notes: Two suspectNames flagged for this matchup ('Land Glacial Prison', 'Use Shapesplitter') are correct Riot names — false positives. Best find here: Inherent Glamour's disguise breaks on immobilizing crowd control, which makes Sejuani a structural counter to Neeko's entire clone game, and it appeared nowhere on the page. Judgement call recorded for review: I removed 'walk behind minions to block Tangle-Barbs'. Riot's text says the tangle roots everything it passes through and grows after passing a champion, which does not support a minion screen — but true minion-collision behaviour is one of the things the kit files explicitly cannot answer, so I replaced the advice with sidestepping rather than asserting that minions do not block it.
